system.name: Welder
system.one_liner: a deep learning compiler that schedules memory access holistically by connecting and scheduling a tile-based data-flow graph across a hierarchical memory abstraction

components.name: DNN Model
components.role: the full input deep learning model

components.name: Tile-graph
components.role: WELDER's data-flow graph of tile-based operators converted from the DNN model

components.name: Tile-graph Scheduler
components.role: schedules the tile-graph by connecting graph regions and scheduling sub-graphs

components.name: Graph Connecting
components.role: connects tile-graph regions ahead of scheduling

components.name: Sub-graph Scheduling
components.role: schedules connected sub-graphs for memory-aware execution

components.name: Tile-graph Scheduling Interface
components.role: common interface exposing scheduling decisions to the memory-hierarchy mapping below

components.name: Hierarchical Tile-Graph on Abstracted Accelerator
components.role: maps the scheduled tile-graph onto an abstracted accelerator's multi-level memory hierarchy

components.name: L0-Mem
components.role: top level of the abstracted accelerator's memory hierarchy

components.name: L1-Mem
components.role: middle level of the abstracted accelerator's memory hierarchy

components.name: L2-Mem
components.role: bottom level of the abstracted accelerator's memory hierarchy

components.name: Hardware Accelerators
components.role: physical hardware the scheduled, memory-mapped tile-graph ultimately runs on

flows.what: WELDER converts the full DNN model into a data-flow graph of tile-based operators
tile-graph handed to the scheduler for graph connecting and sub-graph scheduling
connected graph regions passed to sub-graph scheduling
scheduling decisions exposed through a common interface
scheduled tile-graph mapped onto the abstracted accelerator's L0/L1/L2 memory hierarchy
the mapped, hierarchical tile-graph executed on hardware accelerators

content.key_idea: WELDER converts a full DNN model into a tile-based data-flow graph, schedules it holistically (connecting and scheduling sub-graphs through one interface), and maps the result onto an abstracted accelerator's multi-level memory hierarchy before running it on hardware accelerators.
content.reading_order: Top-down: DNN Model into the Tile-graph, down into the Tile-graph Scheduler (Graph Connecting / Sub-graph Scheduling / its interface), down into the L0/L1/L2 memory hierarchy, down to Hardware Accelerators.

palette.used_for: lighter blue fill for the Graph Connecting box
darker blue fill for the Sub-graph Scheduling box and L1-Mem squares
red squares/arrow highlighting a specific tile mapping in the memory hierarchy
gray L2-Mem squares and generic borders

style.stroke: ~0.46pt, dashed arrow highlighting a tile mapped across L1-Mem
style.arrows: straight arrows with filled heads (32 heads) connecting the layered boxes
style.icons: 7 small icons depicting generic tile-based operator shapes chained together in the Tile-graph

encoding.color_means: blue shades distinguish Graph Connecting from Sub-graph Scheduling; red highlights one tile's placement/movement across the L0/L1/L2 memory hierarchy; gray marks the lowest (L2) memory level
encoding.line_style_means: a red dashed arrow traces how a single tile is mapped/moved across memory levels
encoding.emphasis: stacking the tile-graph, its scheduler, and the memory hierarchy as separate labeled bands emphasizes WELDER's holistic view spanning compute scheduling and memory placement together
reusable_patterns: compiler-stack diagram with input model at top and hardware at bottom, scheduling and memory-hierarchy layers in between

evidence: WELDER takes a full DNN model as input and converts it into a data-flow graph of tile-based

summary: Figure 3 is WELDER's system overview, drawn as a top-down compiler stack. A DNN Model is converted into a Tile-graph, a data-flow graph of tile-based operators (shown as a chain of generic operator icons). The Tile-graph Scheduler then performs Graph Connecting and Sub-graph Scheduling, exposing its decisions through a Tile-graph Scheduling Interface. Below this, the scheduled tile-graph is mapped as a Hierarchical Tile-Graph onto an Abstracted Accelerator's three-level memory hierarchy (L0-Mem, L1-Mem, L2-Mem), with a highlighted red dashed path showing one tile's placement across levels. Finally, this hierarchical, scheduled representation runs on the underlying Hardware Accelerators. The available body text is cut off just after introducing the tile-based data-flow graph, so the deeper mechanics of scheduling and memory mapping are read primarily from the figure's own labels.
